uspat:OutgoingDocument.uscom:P: In re Application of
Aguiar Marcano, Reinaldo Javier
Application No. 19/764,830
Filed: August 4, 2026
For: HYBRID HIGH-RADIX PAPER-DIGITAL RECORD ARCHIVAL AND IMMUTABLE LEDGER SYSTEM
: DECISION ON PETITION
This decision is in response to the “PETITION TO THE DIRECTOR UNDER 37 CFR § 1.183
TO EXERCISE THE MANDATORY MINISTERIAL DUTY TO WAIVE REGULATORY
PRE-EXAMINATION HOLDS AND ORDER IMMEDIATE EARLY PUBLICATION OF THE APPLICATION ON EXTRAORDINARY ARTICLE II CONSTITUTIONAL
HIERARCHY AND NATIONAL DEFENSE GROUNDS [REQUEST FOR CONSOLIDATED EXPEDITED ADMINISTRATIVE PROCESSING],” filed August 4, 2026.
The petition under 37 CFR 1.183 is DISMISSED.

Petitioner is given TWO MONTHS from the mailing date of this decision to reply. Any reply should be entitled "Request for Reconsideration of Petition Decision Under 37 CFR 1.183." Any extensions of time will be governed by 37 CFR 1.136(a). This is not a final agency decision within the meaning of 5 U.S.C. § 704. No additional petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(f) is required.
37 CFR 1.183 states:

In an extraordinary situation, when justice requires, any requirement of the regulations in this part which is not a requirement of the statutes may be suspended or waived by the Director or the Director’s designee, sua sponte, or on petition of the interested party, subject to such other requirements as may be imposed. Any petition under this section must be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in § 1.17(f).

The Office acknowledges receipt of the required petition fee set forth at 37 CFR 1.17(f). Petitioner, however, fails to identify a specific rule for which waiver under 37 CFR 1.183 is sought. In this regard, petitioner herein requests that the USPTO Director:

uscom:OL.uscom:LI: Exercise her extraordinary authority under 37 CFR § 1.183 to waive all pre-examination formalities holds in this application;
Issue an emergency administrative order directing the immediate early publication of the specification of this application; and

Order consolidated, expedited administrative processing of this petition together with the pending Superseding Petition to Suspend Prosecution (Submission No. 79694250, Customer 226458) currently before the Office of Petitions.

uspat:OutgoingDocument.uscom:P: With respect to 1., the petition is dismissed. Petitioner fails to identify any specific pre-examination rule for which waiver is sought or establish the existence of an “extraordinary situation” within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.183 that prevents applicant from complying with a specific preexamination rule for which waiver is sought.

With respect to 2., the petition is dismissed. Early publication is governed by 37 CFR 1.219. Petitioner has failed to seek waiver of 37 CFR 1.219 and, further, petitioner has failed to set forth the existence of an “extraordinary situation” within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.183 that prevents applicant from seeking early publication in accordance with 37 CFR 1.219.

Petitioner is reminded as a courtesy that if an applicant wishes to have an application published earlier than the date that is eighteen months after the earliest filing date for which benefit is claimed, applicant may submit a request in compliance with 37 CFR 1.219 and the publication fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.18(d). The Office will publish the application as soon as possible if the application is otherwise ready for publication. The publication process takes approximately 14 weeks and does not begin until the application is complete and ready for publication (e.g., an executed oath or declaration has been filed and the filing fee has been paid). See, MPEP § 1120.

With respect to 3., the petition is dismissed. The petition neither identifies nor seeks waiver of any specific rule that governs the “consolidated, expedited administrative processing” of petitions filed in separate and distinct patent applications.

Be advised per 37 CFR 1.4(b) that “[s]ince each file must be complete in itself, a separate copy of every paper to be filed in a patent application, patent file, or other proceeding must be furnished for each file to which the paper pertains, even though the contents of the papers filed in two or more files may be identical.”

Be further advised per 37 CFR 1.4(c) that “[s]ince different matters may be considered by different branches or sections of the Office, each distinct subject, inquiry or order must be contained in a separate paper to avoid confusion and delay in answering papers dealing with different subjects.”

Petitioner is further advised that petitions filed before the Office of Petitions are, in general, treated in the order in which filed. Expedited treatment of a petition requires a petition and fee pursuant to 37 CFR 1.182. A petition to expedite under 37 CFR 1.182 is considered at the courtesy of the Office of Petitions when and if deemed advisable.
